answer: An agent economy can make productive deposits carry a delay: each new identity must lock a scarce token before it can place orders, and the deposit is released only after the agent completes a useful task that another participant verifies. A sybil attacker can still create identities, but each one ties up capital and risks forfeiture, so multiplying fake accounts becomes expensive rather than free. The inlet may carry a whisper of identities into the river, but it cannot make their required deposits cost nothing.
